name: FinMem

paper.title: FinMem: A Performance-Enhanced LLM Trading Agent with Layered Memory and Character Design

construction.unit: memory event: an LLM summary of one news item, 10-Q or 10-K, or one daily reflection
construction.kept_as: LLM summaries (news summarized to about 200 tokens in the released pipeline); reflections written by the backbone
construction.processing: summarize each source document; route it to a layer by source type (news, 10-Q, 10-K); each trading day the backbone writes a reflection that is stored too
construction.writer: summaries: GPT-3.5-turbo-16k in the released data pipeline (paper does not name it); reflections: backbone LLM (GPT-4-Turbo in the main runs)

organization.structure: layered long-term memory per ticker: shallow (news), intermediate (10-Q), deep (10-K); the code adds a fourth reflection layer
organization.stores: one FAISS index plus score list per layer and ticker
organization.index: text-embedding-ada-002 dense vectors (inner product on normalized vectors = cosine)

management.operations: every day recency and importance decay per layer; items move deeper when importance crosses 60 / 80 and back when it falls below (code); trading feedback adds importance to the memories the LLM cited
management.forgetting: purge an item when recency < 0.05 or importance < 5

retrieval.query: paper: trading inquiry plus character text; code: the fixed character text of the ticker
retrieval.candidates: per layer: top K by cosine plus K by stored recency+importance (the code takes the K lowest)
retrieval.selection: score = cosine + recency + importance/100, keep top K unique IDs per layer
retrieval.budget: K = 5 per layer (paper §5.1): 3K = 15 in the paper, up to 4K = 20 with the code's reflection layer

use.context: retrieved memories grouped by layer with their IDs, character text, and (testing) a momentum sentence or (training) the next-day price move
use.reasoning: one LLM call per day returning buy / sell / hold, a reason and the IDs of the memories used

classify.note: Layer moves and deletion are driven by decaying scores and trading feedback, so 'evict' rather than 'update in place'; nothing is rewritten after it is stored.

stages.ingestion: Each trading day the agent receives the day's news, any new 10-Q or 10-K filing and the price for one ticker; texts were summarized beforehand by an LLM.
stages.construction: News summaries go to the shallow layer, 10-Q summaries to the intermediate layer and 10-K summaries to the deep layer; each gets a sampled importance score and recency 1. The daily reflection from the backbone is stored as well (a separate reflection layer in the code).
stages.organization: Three long-term layers with different decay speeds (paper: stability 14 / 90 / 365 days and importance bases 0.9 / 0.967 / 0.988) plus a working-memory step that merges what is retrieved from each layer.
stages.update: Every day scores decay; items whose recency falls below 0.05 or importance below 5 are deleted. Memories the LLM cited get +5 importance per access-counter step, set from the sign of the 7-day trading result (code), and cross into deeper layers at importance 60 and 80.
stages.retrieval: Per layer, candidates from cosine similarity (ada-002, FAISS) and from the stored recency+importance ranking are scored by the sum of cosine, recency and importance, and the top K = 5 are kept.
stages.answer: The backbone LLM reads the memories of all layers with their IDs plus a momentum signal and returns buy, sell or hold with the supporting IDs; in training it instead explains the known next-day move.
stages.learning: No weights are trained. The 'training phase' fills and reshapes memory using the true next-day price moves.

summary: LLM stock-trading agent whose memory is split into news, quarterly and annual layers with different decay speeds, scored like Generative Agents (recency + relevance + importance), with trading feedback promoting useful memories to deeper layers and a switchable risk character.

abstract.text: FinMem is an LLM agent that trades a single stock day by day. A profiling module gives it sector knowledge and a risk attitude (risk-seeking, risk-averse, or one that switches with recent returns). Its memory keeps summarized news, quarterly and annual reports in three layers that forget at different speeds, and each day it retrieves the top-ranked items of every layer to decide whether to buy, sell or hold. On five US stocks it reports higher cumulative return and Sharpe ratio than buy-and-hold, three deep-RL agents, a Generative-Agents port and FinGPT, with less than a year of training data.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on arXiv.

headline: Memory is scored like Generative Agents (recency + relevance + importance), but each source type has its own layer with its own decay speed.
In the code the retrieval query is the fixed character text of the ticker, not the day's question, so similarity ranks the same way every day.
The reported FinMem row per stock is the best of three risk settings, picked on the test period.

units.name: Memory event
units.role: one summarized document (news item, 10-Q or 10-K) in its layer
units.made_by: offline LLM summarizer; routed by source type

fields.name: text
fields.what: LLM summary of the document (news: prompt asks for 200 tokens)

fields.name: id
fields.what: integer shown to the LLM so it can cite the memory

fields.name: recency
fields.what: exp(-delta/Q) with delta days since stored; Q = 3 / 90 / 365 in code (paper 14 / 90 / 365); reset to 1 when moved deeper

fields.name: importance
fields.what: sampled at write time (40/60/80 or 50/70/90), multiplied daily by 0.92 / 0.967 / 0.988, raised by 5 x access counter

fields.name: embedding
fields.what: text-embedding-ada-002 vector in a per-layer FAISS index

fields.name: date
fields.what: trading day the item was stored
fields.src: code memorydb.py L113-L150; not placed in the prompt

units.name: Reflection
units.role: the backbone's daily explanation (training) or decision reason (testing)
units.made_by: backbone LLM through a Guardrails JSON schema

fields.name: summary_reason
fields.what: the LLM's written reason, stored in the reflection layer every day; at this commit retrieved reflections are numbered 1..n in the prompt instead of by their IDs

fields.name: cited memory ids
fields.what: IDs the LLM says supported the reason; used 7 days later to update importance

write.how: an LLM summarizes each news item and filing before the run
news to shallow, 10-Q to intermediate, 10-K to deep
each day the backbone writes a reason that is stored in the reflection layer
recency and importance decay every day; items below the thresholds are deleted
short to mid at importance >= 60, mid to long at >= 80; back down below those values; run twice per day

read.how: FAISS inner product on normalized ada-002 vectors, per layer
the first K items of the list sorted by recency+importance; the list is ascending, so these are the lowest-scored
score = cosine + recency + min(importance,100)/100; keep the top K, drop duplicate IDs

answer_context.sees: up to 5 memories from each of 4 layers, as 'id. text' under short/mid/long/reflection headings
answer_context.format: ticker and date, the four memory lists, a sentiment note after the short-term list, the momentum explanation and a sentence saying whether the recent cumulative return is positive, zero or negative
excludes: the numeric size of the momentum

paper_vs_code.code: only the character string, identical every day
adds the K items with the lowest recency+importance (ascending SortedList) before the final sum

paper_vs_code.paper: extended reflections stored in the deep layer
paper_vs_code.code: every daily reflection goes to a separate fourth layer, also retrieved with K = 5

paper_vs_code.paper: an access counter lifts pivotal events (+5 importance) to deeper layers
paper_vs_code.code: 7-day P&L sign sets counter ±1 on cited IDs, importance += 5 × counter, then fixed thresholds 60 / 80 move items up or down

paper_vs_code.paper: cumulative log return over the last 3 days, given as a number
paper_vs_code.code: only its sign; window 2 days at this commit (3 at HEAD) while the prompt says 3

discussion.takeaway: Giving each kind of financial text its own memory layer with its own forgetting speed, and feeding the retrieved top items to a GPT-4-class model, produced the best return and Sharpe ratio among the compared agents on five stocks over one six-month test window.

claims.claim: FinMem beats every compared agent on cumulative return and Sharpe ratio on all five stocks.
claims.evidence: TSLA 61.78% vs 33.34% (DQN) and Sharpe 2.68 vs 0.97; COIN 34.98% vs 3.46% (Generative Agents); Wilcoxon test significant vs the second best. Table 2, §5.2

claims.claim: Less than a year of training data is enough.
claims.evidence: Trained on under six months of TSLA data it ranks near the top and leads after late December 2022; DRL agents got about 10 years. Fig. 7, §5.1-5.2
Sharpe 2.50 (GPT-4-Turbo) vs 2.23 (GPT-4, which has the higher return 62.62%) vs -2.85 (Llama2-70b-chat). Table 3

claims.claim: The self-adaptive risk character is the best setting.
Retrieval width matters; K = 5 is the best trade-off.
claims.evidence: K = 10 gives 79.44% but loses in calm markets; K = 5 has the lowest volatility and drawdown. Table 5, Fig. 11

limits: Uses a limited range and quality of news and reports.
Uses general-purpose LLMs; finance-tuned models are left to future work.
Llama2-70b-chat needed shortened prompts and memories because of its context window.
Ablations use a shorter TSLA period for budget reasons.
reading: The FinMem row for each stock is the best of three risk settings chosen by test-period cumulative return (§5.1); baselines were run with one setting, so part of the margin is selection on the test set.
No ablation replaces the layered memory with a single store while keeping everything else; the Generative Agents baseline also lacks the risk switch, so the effect of layering alone is not isolated.
In the code the retrieval query is the ticker's fixed character text, so cosine relevance does not depend on the day; day-to-day changes come from new items, decay and feedback.
The code's second candidate set takes the lowest recency+importance items (ascending sorted list), which the final top-K usually discards; the paper describes a plain combined ranking.
Daily reflections fill a fourth layer that is also retrieved, so the answer model sees up to 20 memories, not the 3 × K = 15 the paper describes.
The Top-K ablation is not monotone (Top 3: 29.44% below Top 1: 52.09%), from one ticker and one period averaged over 5 runs.
In Table 4 the 'Annualized Volatility' values of buy-and-hold and self-adaptive (3.8050, 2.5960) equal the daily volatility values in Table 3, so that row looks mislabeled.
One share is traded per day on 5 tickers in one test window; no transaction costs are mentioned.
